builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SKILL2STEER: One-Pass Hypernetwork for Mapping Natural-Language Skills to Low-Rank Post-Block Activation Shifts
summary: It replaces keeping natural-language skill instructions in the prompt (and, relative to per-skill weight adapters, replaces weight-space adaptation) by compiling a skill document once into low-rank post-block activation shifts while keeping base weights frozen and running the hypernetwork only at compile time. It costs an additional compile-time hypernetwork pass plus a small per-skill artifact (2.36M parameters) and requires integrating activation-shift injection at every decoder block (optionally scheduled across retrieval steps), with routing-free deployment possible as a single averaged bundle. It can fail because the learned shift may encode a domain-general behavioural prior rather than the skill content (wrong skill text can perform on par), so behaviour can change without delivering the intended skill-specific semantics and may be sensitive to domain shift, scheduling, and deployment details.
rationale: The approach is small enough for constrained infrastructure, but the reported controls show the injected direction may not carry skill content, so production adoption should be gated by workload-specific validation.

claims.statement: It replaces keeping natural-language skill instructions in the prompt (and, relative to per-skill weight adapters, replaces weight-space adaptation) by compiling a skill document once into low-rank post-block activation shifts while keeping base weights frozen and running the hypernetwork only at compile time. It costs an additional compile-time hypernetwork pass plus a small per-skill artifact (2.36M parameters) and requires integrating activation-shift injection at every decoder block (optionally scheduled across retrieval steps), with routing-free deployment possible as a single averaged bundle. It can fail because the learned shift may encode a domain-general behavioural prior rather than the skill content (wrong skill text can perform on par), so behaviour can change without delivering the intended skill-specific semantics and may be sensitive to domain shift, scheduling, and deployment details.

On SearchQA, a seven-dataset benchmark, the method reaches 37.9 exact match, 9.8 points above the frozen model and 2.3 points above a weight-space adapter, while compiling each skill to 2.36M parameters (9.25x fewer than the weight-space adapter).
